title: Skoropadskyi's Coup
desc:
Due to Oleksandr Ohloblyn's unpopular policies and obvious signs of collaboration with the nazis, in particular, aiding and abetting in racial cleansing-the mass extermination of the Jewish population during World War II in Babyn Yar-and his clear dictatorial tendencies, Danylo Skoropadskyi, a descendant of the last hetman of Ukraine, Pavlo Skoropadsky, with the support of the free Cossack troops and the direct assistance of Stus's United Struggle faction, arrested the elected president on suspicion of treason...

Now only Danylo will decide the next years of an entire nation that has placed its trust in the hetman. Step by step, plan by plan, brick by brick, Ukraine will rise like a phoenix from the ashes of ruin. The UHS will surpass all other political forces in building a new, strong, globally important Ukrainian Hetmanate!

title: Skoropadskyi Strikes Back!
desc:
Dziuba couldn't believe it. The situation had quickly spiraled out of his control. It was all over. He should have foreseen the consequences of starting repressions against the fascists. It was one thing when all failures could be blamed on the controversial Ohloblyn, but it was quite another when it came to a respected general in the army, a hero of the civil war, and Stus's right-hand man.

Taras Bulba-Borovets refused to submit to our repressive policy against despotism in the country, and together with Stus and Danylo Skoropadskyi, they formed a coalition, supported by 80% of our army, and are already demanding in front of the government building on Khreshchatyk in Kyiv that Ivan Dziuba renounce all presidential powers granted to him by the people.

If he agrees to the military's demands, he will face life-long house arrest somewhere in Bila Tserkva, but if he refuses, citing his right to continue performing presidential functions, he will be arrested and imprisoned.So he chose the path of freedom and voluntarily renounced the position of President of the Ukrainian People Republic.

However, when Stus arrived at the parliament to take the oath, Danylo Skoropadskyi appeared with loyal, well-armed units of the "Free Cossacks". He announced to the entire parliament that from now on he would become the Hetman-leader of the new Ukrainian Hetmanate, and anyone who did not agree with this would be immediately thrown out into the street and stripped of all ranks, like useless trash. The first to recognize the new Hetman was General Taras Bulba-Borovets, because he saw in him the energy and salvation that the Ukrainian land had been waiting for so long. Vasyl Stus agreed only on the condition that he be given the status of Prime Minister in the Hetmanate.

title: The Fate of the Dniester and Bug Administration
desc:
It was a special report for Danylo Skoropadskyi, concerning Transnistria, or more precisely, the occupied part of Vinnytsia and the entire Odessa region, together with the former Moldovan autonomous region of Transnistria within the Ukrainian SSR.

Indeed, these ethnically Ukrainian lands are a strategic hub for trade on the Danube, and the port city of Odessa serves as the most important transport and trade hub in the Black Sea, the importance of which cannot be overestimated.In short, we have acquired a real territorial treasure, and now we are faced with the task of deciding the future fate of these lands right now.

There are two strategies that our ministers have encountered. This region, half destroyed by war, is teeming with rebellious Romanians, Moldovans, Germans, and Greeks who refuse to obey the new authorities. These minorities, which have grown in number over more than two decades of occupation, make up half of the region's population, and we will have to deal with them right now. In another scenario, we will pass these problems on to the Dniester and Bug Administrations so that they can persuade these settlers to live in peace and harmony with Ukrainians, or to move to Romania under the "suitcase-train station-Bucharest" program.

These two options are equally effective, and it is up to Hetman Danylo to decide whether it is better to assimilate the locals into our state and personally restore the region's economy, or to shift this burden onto our puppet government.

title: Final Full Integration of Transnistria
desc:
More than a year after the defeat of the Romanians and Germans in the Transnistrian Civil War, it seems that the local administration has finally managed to pacify the region. All that remains is to consolidate our success, restore the long-lost administrative and territorial apparatus by dividing the region into three provinces within the Hetmanate, and integrate local troops into the Armed Forces of Hetmanate.

Although a small number of Romanian terrorists still remain in the Transnistrian region, information about their cells and places of uncontrolled border crossing with Romania has been provided to us by loyal local residents and the local administration. We expect the region to finally calm down in the coming months.

It's time to build trade ties through Odessa. First, we'll get in touch with Turkey so they give us free passage for trade ships through the Bosphorus Strait, and also with the Italian-Egyptian protectorate so our ships can go through the Suez Canal. From now on, we're part of the global trading community!

title: First Time In First Grade
desc:
It was a special and long-awaited day for Petro, because finally, after the reconstruction of the once prestigious elite school in Kyiv, which had been closed for several years, he could continue his education without hindrance.Thanks to the efforts of the local city administration, with state investment, a massive restoration of schools across the country has begun.

Galina, the boy's mother, packed the necessary school supplies into his backpack and gave him a generous allowance for the week to donate to further repairs and purchases of books, Ukrainian literature, and educational textbooks for the school. In these post-war times, decades of occupation have resulted in significant illiteracy among the local population. Although teachers were selected based on passing an exam demonstrating sufficient knowledge of their subject, especially fluency in the Ukrainian language, there were cases of teachers lacking experience compared to teachers in other European countries.Wishing him all the best, Galina asked her son to study so that his father would always be proud of him.

Due to traffic problems, the boy was late to the bus station and ended up being the last to arrive in class. All the other first-graders were already sitting at their desks, and the homeroom teacher was trying to keep the class quiet and orderly until the last pupil arrived. Carefully opening the door to the sunlit classroom and seeing his homeroom teacher, Oksana Volodymyrivna, the boy apologized for being late and expressed his gratitude that the others had waited for him. Oksana Volodymyrivna invited her last pupil to the center of the classroom and said; 

- "Childrens, this is your 14th and last classmate, Petro. Please treat him with respect, kindness, and honor so that our class becomes the friendliest group in our school!

title: Support for ROA?
desc:
Since we are currently continuing to work closely with reformist nazis, why not use the same approach with other forces that have dealt with them in the past, such as the ROA(Russian Liberation Army)? At present, we do not have sufficient information about these reformers and do not know their motives, which poses the risk that they may deceive us and drive us into even greater dependence from Germania. At the same time, decisive opposition to their intentions will result in us losing the support of the german elite, so what should we do?

In fact, the hetman was not the only one in this position. ROA general Andrey Vlasov is also in similar conditions in the east, the leader of the russian warlord state, located mostly near Samara city, had to deal with germans most part of post-war period. Danylo, no matter how much he hated the bolsheviks, was ready to compromise with Russian collaborators at a time when it was so necessary for the Hetmanate. Although the general already had one foot in the grave, Vlasov sent a reply from his capital in Samara, agreeing to provide all the details of his flirtations over the years with all supporters of nazi ideology in exchange for comprehensive assistance.

The essence of the agreement is the permanent presence of the Hetmanate volunteer corps in case of wars by the ROA for the unification of Russia. As soon as the ROA unifies Russia, the Hetmanate will be able to recall the volunteer contingent back to Ukraine. In return, former Russian collaborators promise to immediately recognize Ukrainian Hetmanate independence and, after unification, to begin fruitful cooperation aimed at developing a non-german economic sphere of influence in Europe, Asia, and other countries. In addition to this, we should consider the benefits for our newly formed armed forces of studying mountain warfare in the Urals, warfare in the swamps and cold tundras of Siberia, and warfare in conditions of lack of infrastructure in the Far East of Russia.

In Danylo's personal opinion, russian wars for unification with the support of one of the most attractive forces for the hetmanist movement, the ROA, will be beneficial in the long term. Although there are fears in the government that after the death of Vlasov, his successor will not want to confront the Nazis and will ultimately refuse to fulfill the agreements after the unification of Russia. Now all that remains is to weigh all the options and make a final decision...

title: Results of the Second Year of the "Breadbasket" Program
desc:
"The new year of our extremely useful program for society continues to develop and exceed our expectations from last year.

The time has come when our Ukrainian individual farmers are able to independently manage their farms and profit from them. Food produced on agricultural land, in villages, and in state cooperatives is sold on the market, and a significant percentage of these transactions goes to the budget. However, the costs of developing agricultural entrepreneurship are not low.

It's also impossible not to notice periodic monthly jumps in inflation, which isn't and won't be stable, so it is necessary to be cautious about investments, possibly limiting them for some time. The problem of increasing ukrainian consumption of grain crops and other foodstuffs is becoming more and more acute. The state's task is to at least maintain parity between food production and consumption, so that it is not necessary to purchase foreign products.

Despite the constant increase in annual consumption demands of the population, our economy continues to grow rapidly. Our ministry has prepared a new action program to combat inflation, but in return we will be forced to reduce state support for agricultural cooperatives."

- With respect to His Excellency the Hetman, Minister of the "BreadBasket" Program, Mykhailo Starozhetskyi.

title: Results of the First Year of the "Breadbasket" Program
desc:
"The first year of consumer spending since the start of state subsidies for the ukrainian agricultural sector has passed, and the first results are already visible. According to statistics, we have improved agricultural production methods, increased our grain reserves, and it appears that they have almost covered all of our national needs.

However, the process of eliminating external influence on our domestic food security sector is still far from its logical conclusion. We hope that in a few years we will be able to fully and, most importantly, independently feed our large and ever-growing population, despite the restrictions of the Second Treaty of the Brest-Litowsk Agreement.

There are many other positive aspects of the state program "BreadBasket". The main one is the increase in local GDP in the regions, which contributes to the growth of the economic power and independence of the Hetmanate. In addition, we can highlight the creation of thousands of new jobs, mainly in villages, as well as the prospects for selling our products to our neighbors, and in a few years, to all of Europe and beyond!

However, we are currently facing difficulties in providing all our citizens with basic necessities, such as insufficient supply of products to remote areas, including Crimea, due to logistical problems. We recommend increasing the size of the garrison on the peninsula due to a new wave of "bread protests" by dissatisfied local radical germans over our prioritization of feeding ukrainians first." 

- With respect to His Excellency the Hetman, Minister of the "BreadBasket" Program, Mykhailo Starozhetskyi.

title: First Incredible Five-Year Result of the "BreadBasket" Program
desc:
"The fifth year of our program marks the beginning of a "golden age" for ukrainian farming. We easily meet the needs of our entire population and earn millions in revenue by trading our products with many European countries. The British Isles, Scandinavia (especially Finland), the Iberian Peninsula, and the Balkans are our regular trading partners, and that's not even the full list!

Our state control over agricultural cooperatives has expanded to entire regions, so we are seeing unprecedented centralization of farming. Farmers and agrarians, although they make significant profits, give half to the state, and the state redirects these funds to increase national and regional GDP. Both sides are satisfied, which creates such a desirable harmony in Ukrainian society!

Next, we plan to expand our trade networks to a global scale. Thanks to the nearly completed construction of a trade hub that will begin in the port of Sevastopol, in a year we will open profitable trade routes with Africa, both Americas, and Asia. In the near future, in just 5-10 years, we will not lag behind the leading countries - the USA or Japan - economically, but will catch up with them! Glory to the Hetmanate, long live Skoropadsky!"

- With respect to His Excellency the Hetman, Minister of the "BreadBasket" Program, Mykhailo Starozhetskyi.

title: Choosing a conflict strategy
desc:
Now we have a unique opportunity to settle scores with hungarian imperialism in the ukrainian carpathian movement. title: New Years of the Greater Ukrainian Hetmanate!
desc:
Finally, Hetman Danylo has a free week in his schedule, which he can use for himself. In recent years, with his coming to power at the end of 1964, such moments were rare, because it was necessary to rebuild the country and fight for its glory in the whole world. But, it seems, all this was achieved and finally Danylo could really be proud of himself and the restored and dominant hetmanists movement in society.

The whole country celebrated the reunification of the country under the banner of the Greater Ukrainian Hetmanate, and even the people of Kuban are beginning to believe in a better tomorrow. The New Year of 1972 was the most lavishly celebrated in the last half century, the New Year tree was put up in all district town centers, people caroled for Christmas, all with full stomachs. Indeed, the Ukrainian decade of the 1970s in Eastern Europe has arrived!

The hetmanist affair will not only continue its course, it will be able to develop further even without the direct participation of Danylo. He decided to celebrate the New Year in the ukrainian Carpathians, together with a diaspora of supporters. He began his 5-day vacation with a tour from Ternopil to Ivano-Frankivsk, visiting villages as well. After making sure that the post-war reconstruction was completed in whole western regions, he stayed for a few days in the best luxury hotel in Yaremcha city. On the 3rd day he visited a bathhouse and on the 4th he visited the hot springs near his hotel. Fully satisfied and refreshed by the local service, on the 5th day he went back to the capital Kyiv city.

A festive atmosphere was in the air after he proclaimed the Greater Ukrainian Hetmanate. Not only the capital, the whole country glorified his power, and those small opposition political elements, including Vasyl Stus, were convinced of the hetman's ability to preserve Ukraine, accepting the hetman's cause and joining this movement.

"Would my father be proud of me now, if he were alive, whose work I realized to the fullest extent only now, in the early 1970's?" - Danylo Skoropadskyi said aloud to himself, going to bed.

title: Danylo's Personality Cult with Unlimited Power
desc:
Hesitating for a long time and considering this step for several months alone, without consulting anyone, Danylo Skoropadskyi decided to obtain unlimited legislative and executive power for himself alone. The threatening international situation and the tense situation in the political space prompt us to take a difficult step. The competition of democratic forces appeared, fed up with military defeats and Hetman's authoritarian-fascist policy in recent years.

Although in general, despite several defeats in proxy conflicts, the army keeps its oath of loyalty to the Ukrainian Hetmanate, despite the protests of civilians, because they believe in Skoropadskyi's ability to skillfully manage and preserve ukrainian statehood, even under the conditions of restrictions on the rights and freedoms of the civilian population, media censorship and the appointment of key ministers at their own discretion. Skoropadskyi relied on this in his decision, concentrating all the levers of Ukrainian Hetmanate management in his hands.

Vasyl Stus, the former right-hand man of the Hetman, announced his disagreement with the concentration of all power in the hands of one person, and together with his supporters in the parliament demanded the abolition of these powers. However, this opposition was detained directly in the parliament by units of the "Free Cossacks". For these dissident actions aimed at harming the hetmanist cause, Vasyl Stus was sent under house arrest with a ban on public and political activities, and other influential supporters of his received prison terms from 1 to 6 years.

The period of dictatorial winter has begun in the Ukrainian Hetmanate, and from now on ukrainians do not know what to expect for tomorrow with the crackdown on demonstrations and peaceful protests.

"Is it worth it, will the ukrainians understand my decision, or will they just distance themselves from me?" - said Danylo Skoropadskyi in his voice, sitting in his office, turning on his radio, trying to calm his nerves with modern ukrainian music.

title: Odesa Demonstrations
desc:
Unprecedented events in the authoritarian Hetmanate have sent shockwaves through all national media outlets, including state-run ones, which are subject to strict censorship. News of the events currently unfolding in the country's main commercial port city - Odesa - is spreading rapidly across the information landscape. Despite the region's recent liberation from Romanian occupation, our state is now facing organized protests in the city itself for the first time. The city's status-quo had been maintained all these years, as we invested significant funds in rebuilding the city, which had been destroyed by fighting. And as soon as we restored it, the global oil crisis began, which brought the entire local transportation network to a halt - an unprecedented display of incompetence on the part of the administration we had established. Until then, the mayor of the city was Serhiy Stepanovych Kotenko, who had obtained the position through "connections".

Due to such shenanigans, in the midst of workers' demonstrations - which were attended by the head of government and acting Prime Minister Andriy Bilopolskyi himself - he announced the dismissal of the incompetent minister. A compromise was needed, even with workers who had not been brainwashed by socialist propaganda; they were citizens of the country just like civil servants. Mr. Andriy wanted to be close to the people, even those who were not ideologically loyal, having recently been freed from Romanian domination and a repressive regime. Accordingly, with the intention of resolving the situation and reaching any possible compromises with the demonstrators, the announcement was made regarding the dismissal of Serhiy Kotenko. Half the crowd, upon hearing this, naturally asked:

"And who will fill the vacant position? Another bureaucrat from the distant capital, who couldn't care less about our localproblems?"

This was followed by a decisive response from the minister.

"We have selected for you a candidate who is a skilled sailor and has been living here for a long time - none other than Tsiurupa Pavlo Andriyovych!"

As expected, the crowd was satisfied with the response, since most were aware of Pavlo's charitable efforts to rebuild the city. Additionally, he had visited the city on multiple occasions since the onset of the oil crisis, consulting with industrialists and business leaders, including visits to newly opened factories producing essential goods and light industrial products. The demonstrators generally spoke positively of him and were already satisfied with what they considered to be a sound personnel decision. Some of the protesters' demands regarding expanded local self-government were not met, as the authorities remained concerned about protest sentiment in the region. Of course, there is no longer any question of military control over Odesa and neighboring regions, but all heads of these territories are strictly selected from the Dnieper region of Ukraine. According to various forecasts, a civilian administration drawn from the local population will begin to take shape over the next 8–12 years in order to eliminate the risk of separatism, which has not yet subsided.

title: The Peninsula's Logistics Woes
desc:
As we navigate the most difficult phase of the oil crisis, our Hetmanate faces many challenges of a national nature. While both the west and the east are holding together and helping one another - thanks to the Ministry of Culture - the same cannot be said for the south. A severe socio-economic crisis is unfolding, further exacerbated by rising gasoline and fuel prices, which in turn are complicating transportation links. Our police departments have already received a dozen reports of various crimes, ranging from purely economic to even criminal. Significantly, these crimes are mostly committed by Germans against Ukrainians and Tatars in the region, which further entrenches anti-German sentiment in our society!

And this problem must be addressed by resolving all disputes involving such individuals - especially those of different nationalities - exclusively through the courts. During the oil crisis, our merchant ships and oil tankers stopped sailing through the Azov Sea, which consumes scarce fuel. Transporting thousands of barrels is complicated by infrastructure issues, as the Crimean Peninsula is not as developed as our other regions. In some places, Crimea is not logistically connected to our country at all (the Arabat Spit) due to constant sabotage by the German resistance movement. Given the difficulty of unloading goods in Mykolaiv, which is simply not equipped to handle the scale of cargo unloading we require, we continue to use Sevastopol and Kerch.

First and foremost, the Hetman instructed his government to resolve the logistical issues and to set aside inefficient maritime trade transportation as a low priority. Along with addressing the land transportation and logistics challenges, cultural and educational initiatives will be carried out among the population of the south, following the precedent of successful efforts throughout Ukraine. Above all, we will strive to meet the needs of everyone - the residents of Kherson, Melitopol, Mariupol, and, of course, Crimea itself. To this end, we will artificially lower local fuel prices without reducing the price for the entire country. All these measures will be unfair and financially challenging in the short term and will not help us quickly overcome the oil crisis. However, in the long term - and even in the medium term, within the next year - we will restore the pre-crisis fuel situation, produce more domestic oil, transport it by sea for trade, and, as a result, emerge from the crisis as a more stable country than we were before it!

title: Flights of Foreigners
desc:
As time has passed since the Hetman of all Ukraine assumed dictatorial, unlimited powers, the domestic situation has changed very little. Although Ukrainians managed for a time to unite their efforts to overcome the oil crisis, which affected all segments of society, everything is returning to the way it was. A new wave of protests against The Hetman's Cause is beginning, and the parliament - which until recently was loyal - can no longer smoothly pass new government agendas. Among the significant difficulties, it is worth noting the parliament's refusal to grant expanded powers to the police to disperse riots; such a vote has already been rejected twice.

It should be noted that it is not only our coalition "partners" who are blocking such resolutions, but also our own collaborators - the parliament is not functioning properly. Our law enforcement agencies are unable to forcibly disperse protests, as they lack authorization to do so from both the government and the regional governors. All we are currently doing to counter this new wave of discontent is blocking roads, railways, and airports to prevent protesters from accessing them. Our Armed Forces of the Hetmanate, which remain loyal to the ideals of the Hetmanist Movement, are also increasingly involved in this process.

The country continues to go about its quiet life, but no one knows how long this status quo will last. At the capital's main airport, Boryspil International Airport (which began operating back in 1961, during the German occupation), German workers, businesspeople, and members of the elite are arriving in increasing numbers under quota arrangements. Flying on Lufthansa's reliable Boeing 737-100 aircraft, between 1500 and 7500 such individuals arrive each month, according to various estimates. The Ukrainian Hetmanate does not oppose their voluntary labor, which, according to various estimates, contributes between 2% and 8% of the state's revenue relative to GDP. title: Yalta Summit
desc:
In order to strengthen ties with the Russian Republic - which was established in the territory of the former Russian Anarchy, not without our help, of course - we held the Yalta Summit. Officially, it is a non-political platform for concluding mutually beneficial agreements and establishing trade relations with the countries of Central Asia and Russia. But in reality, this event will likely be a defining moment in the new Eurasian geopolitics. As the Greater Ukrainian Hetmanate drifts further and further away from the Reich's sphere of influence, this poses many risks to our security. We must not be left alone to face this savage beast, for all our efforts to strengthen Ukraine's position must not be in vain!

Alongside several delegations from Central Asia - including representatives of the Kazakh anti-Bolshevik intelligentsia - a significant delegation from the Russian Republic was also present. With Russia's recent unification - which took place just a decade ago - they cast a shadow over all the other summit participants. The Russians are represented by Georgy Zhilenikov - Bunyachenko's right-hand man and trusted confidant - who did not arrive here by chance. The Russian Liberation Army remembers the assistance provided by the Hetmanist forces during such critical times of active and persistent efforts to reunify Russia. Following their success, President [SAM.GetLeader] has indeed decided to honor the terms of bilateral commitments and is inviting our country to join the Collective Security Bloc! Here is the letter the Hetman personally received from him:

"I wish good health to His Excellency the Hetman, and to my unquestionable ally in the anti-Bolshevik struggle, [FUK.GetLeader]! I am writing to you to express my gratitude for your timely and vital assistance and for the contribution your Hetmanist Movement has made to the unification of Russia. We are ready to fulfill the obligations entrusted to us: to recognize your Greater Ukrainian Hetmanate within its current borders, to continue working closely together to overcome the dominant Unity Pact in Europe, and to admit you into the Collective Security Bloc at the earliest opportunity! Furthermore, my Prime Minister Zhilenikov has been briefed on the relevant instructions and will formally accept any declarations of friendship and strategic partnership for an indefinite term from your side at the official level. May the historic friendship between White Russia and the centralized Ukraine endure forever with the defeat of the Nazi scourge in Europe and Asia, wherever they may be. Glory to Russia and the Hetmanate!" - the end of [SAM.GetLeader]'s personal letter. After rereading it, Danylo called Bilopolskyi, who happened to be at the Yalta summit at that very moment.

The Hetman did not want to make the same mistake again, for he knew the reasons behind the Whites' defeat in the former Russian Civil War. Even today, not all of the army - nor even the generals of the Russian Liberation Army - viewed the existence of an independent Ukraine favorably. But the current realities were simply pushing both sides toward an understanding. The coming years would be decisive for all of Europe; all the Hetman's men understood this after the proclamation of the Greater Ukrainian Hetmanate. The question was framed differently: "What if the Reich strikes the Hetmanate first?" or "What if the Russia loses again, will we be left alone after that against the Nazi eagle in a helpless situation?"

In any case, the minister was on the phone, awaiting Danylo's final decision. Having gathered his strength to once again recount the tragic history of cooperation with the Russians, and guided first and foremost by the interests of Ukrainian statehood, the order was given...

title: Cossacks in the High Castle
desc:
Stores and businesses were open, the metallurgical and industrial sectors were producing materials, and the population and the army were working to ensure the stability of the Hetmanate. A little over eight years have passed since the Hetmanist Coup, and the scent of a new war is closer than ever. Just as we did seven years ago, we risk once again finding ourselves in a stalemate against the Greater Germanic Reich, which dominates Europe. Just like the weak and lone David against the mighty Goliath...

But that is not the case; our Ukrainian people are confident: if the Reich and Führer [GER.GetLeader] have not yet attacked us, it means they lack the strength to do so. The Nazis understand that if they dare to do so, it would directly threaten their food security. Under the Second Treaty of Brest-Litowsk, we continue to supply them with food in exchange for peace between our two countries. This is a kind of precautionary - and, in some ways, manipulative - tool in bilateral relations, used by both sides. It is not 100% beneficial to anyone, so its continued existence in its current form is impossible. Although German bureaucrats are trying to find alternative sources of food - such as the vast expanse of France - everything ultimately comes down to Ukraine's fertile black soil.

But our Ukrainian agricultural sector is not standing still; it, too, is constantly improving. The full mechanization of agriculture is already 75% complete, and our diplomats are successfully introducing the latest Japanese technologies to boost agricultural production. Our fields are more productive than ever; perhaps this is what is currently preventing the Wehrmacht from destroying its former "Breadbasket" in the flames of destructive war. But that is the situation as of today, for with the unification of Russia and the conflicts in France, more and more new threats are emerging for the German New Order. The world does not stand still, unlike the Reich, so we have every chance of defeating Goliath; we just need to wait for the right moment - or strike first, without waiting for a response from Germania.

In the coming year, [FUK.GetLeader] must find as many partners and allies for Ukraine as possible if he plans to preserve Ukrainian statehood. After all, a future large-scale war is no longer a mere possibility - it is a fully realistic scenario for the Greater Ukrainian Hetmanate. If the Hetman's followers seek to save their homeland from destruction, they will either become even stronger than they were yesterday, or they will be perish - along with independent Ukraine - perhaps forever...

desc:

What began as rumors and inconclusive intelligence reports from the Reichskommissariat Moskowien authorities has finally made waves across Europe, particularly in Ukraine. The news is simple, yet terrifying - the Russians are amassing massive, colossal armed forces along the German-Russian border.

The choice now is what position we will take in this inevitable, bloody war. After all, if we remain within the German sphere of influence, we risk being directly drawn into the eastern meat grinder. And given the numerous losses already suffered by the current generation of Ukrainians, it would be better to stay on the sidelines. This is Hetman's view; however, many military leaders warn of the danger of a second betrayal of the Germans - which Germania will certainly not forgive. Moreover, we must take into account that this will be a war between nuclear powers, so each side will destroy anyone who is directly on the enemy's side. Therefore, by choosing neutrality and betraying the Germans, we will be left on our own, surrounded by enemies - both the eastern barbarians and the beasts from the west.

desc:

title: Plebiszit in Galizien?
desc:
On this ordinary working morning, Albert Speer, Führer of the Greater Germanic Reich, pored over a report sent by his diplomats from Kyiv. Yes, that's right, Skoropadsky's Hetman government had requested a "plebiscite" in Galicia. In reality, it was offering billions of marks in exchange for the transfer of Galicia, granting it autonomous status with free and unrestricted activity for German megacorporations.

Although this decision would undoubtedly allow us to finance the rapid restoration of the country and get rid of the scars of war in the short term, Speyer understood the risks of agreeing to such a "plebiscite".These hetmans may perceive this as both weakness and mercy. However, by agreeing to these conditions, we will be able to lull the belligerence of these cossacks and get rid of the hidden hostile sentiments of Ukrainian slaves with one concession. The rebels have shown how easily they can overthrow our local administrations during any German crisis. In addition, the transfer of all of Galicia to the Ukrainians, which the crushed Poles still claim, will allow us to further quarrel these two nations and distance ourselves from their hatred towards us.In this way, we will get rid of ethnic problems in the Reich.

However, the Führer's report contained another request from Danylo Skoropadskyi himself. In an additional letter, he pledged to continue payments for Galicia and the remnants of the Reichskommissariat Ukraine, because, in his words, "Ukraine, as a European state, should not be divided between two competing governments".Albert did not know how to respond to this request. A week passed, and all of his reichsministers asked him to refuse Skoropadsky's request to transfer Brest, but why mistakenly cling to something that had proven unviable without the help of the Reich?If the Reichskommissariat turned out to be such a corrupt structure that it failed to suppress poorly armed rebels, what would prevent those same rebels from finishing what they had started and finally eliminating the remnants of the Reichskommissariat Ukraine?The final answer remains with the new Führer himself.

This absurd reality, which even the Greater Germanic Reich could not have imagined, has finally come to pass thanks to Skoropadsky's thoughtful and purposeful policy of undermining German influence in Eastern Europe. However, there are currently no direct signs of a military response from Führer Bormann to the creation of an empire that does not obey the established New Order, due to the consequences of the oil crisis.

The Reich has already applied all possible economic sanctions against the Hetmanate to exacerbate the local crisis. Whether the Hetman will dare to renounce the Second treaty of Brest-Litowsk or not, only time will tell.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Danylo Establishes a Personal Dictatorship!
desc:
The latest news has shocked the ukrainian diaspora around the world. What began as a "pro-ukrainian authoritarianism with controlled parliamentarism" has now turned into an open fascist authoritarian dictatorship built on the cult of personality of Danylo Skoropadskyi.

After the unexpected end of the UHS coalition with United Struggle and the arrest of it's leader Vasyl Stus, as well as the closure of parliament, Hetmanate has de-facto become a truly dictatorship, completely controlled by one person. There are reports of protests and demonstrations in Kyiv, Kharkiv, Dnipro, Vinnytsia, Lutsk against the dissolution of parliament. However, these actions are quickly suppressed by the Special Department and the Free Cossack troops.

Given the rapid and widespread arrests of prominent political opponents, republican agitators, independently journalists, as well as the complete state control over the AFH, the likelihood of removing the hetman from power is negligible.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]Successful Tests of Russian Nuclear Weapons
desc:
Unexpectedly for everyone, German sailors, who have bases and access to the controlled archipelago of Novaya Zemlya, will report an unknown spike in radiation levels in the local air. Based on the analysis and wind direction, it was determined that the epicenter of the explosion was the coastal area near the Arctic Ocean - Salekhard. A few hours later, it becomes clear that the now reunited Russia has finally acquired weapons of mass destruction...

Since few in the world believed in the ability of some warlord in Russian anarchy to unite Russia, let alone research and test its own nuclear weapons in such a short time, now all of humanity is truly living for today. With the emergence of a new nuclear power on the world stage, and such an unreliable player in the form of a unified Russia, the world has once again entered a tense period of uncertainty. Germania and Tokyo have already officially condemned the successful testing of nuclear weapons, threatening to impose numerous sanctions on the new competitor if it doesn't stop the further accumulation of new strategic weapons.
